question: Viewing 20 flats in turn, each accepted or refused on the spot: by the 37% rule, how many do you refuse first?
move: Look long enough to learn the range, then take the first that beats it.
ask: In the choice I keep putting off, have I already seen enough options to know what good looks like?
trap: Viewing all 20 first, though the early ones are gone once refused.
hint: Take 37% of the total, round down, then pick the first flat better than all of those.
steps: Round down: view and refuse the first 7.
Then take the first flat better than all 7: even so, this finds the very best only about 38% of the time.
reference: Ferguson, Who Solved the Secretary Problem?, Statistical Science, 1989
